title: Generative-model design and simulation
description: State a model's assumptions, variables and outputs; implement or inspect its simulator; generate labelled synthetic observations; check the simulated behaviour matches the intended task; keep the description and the simulator from diverging.

title: Parameter estimation and uncertainty
description: The likelihood or objective, its constraints and the estimation procedure; sensitivity to initialisation; reporting uncertainty; recognising when fitted values are not uniquely informative.

title: Parameter recovery
description: Simulating with known parameters, refitting and comparing true and recovered values across more than one setting and data quantity, reporting systematic errors rather than relying on one convenient correlation.

title: Model recovery and model comparison
description: Simulating from competing models, fitting all candidates, applying a stated comparison procedure, inspecting confusion, and interpreting non-discrimination as a result.

title: Predictive and simulation checks
description: Comparing predictions with relevant observed or simulated patterns, naming the held-out unit, inspecting leakage, using a meaningful baseline, and stating the validation question behind any claim that a model is validated.

title: Measurement reliability and validity
description: Distinguishing an average experimental effect, ranking differences between people, within-person change, practice effects, stability across occasions, the interpretation of a score and its proposed use.

title: Longitudinal and transfer evaluation
description: Held-out trials, people, tasks and later time periods as different generalisation questions; what information is available at prediction time; chronology-aware evaluation that never leaks later information into an earlier prediction.

title: Scientific argument from models
description: Distinguishing fitting a pattern, predicting new observations, supporting a mechanism, identifying a causal effect and supporting an application claim; valuing stated limits and well-supported negative findings.

title: Model-based planning versus cached policies
description: Search over an internal model of states, actions and outcomes compared with a cached action policy learned from experience; what each predicts when the world changes.

title: Transfer, detours and revaluation
description: Tests in which the task changes after learning (a blocked path, a new shortcut, a revalued goal) and why the first decisions after the change carry most of the evidence about strategy.

title: Learning and choice models for bandit tasks
description: Rescorla-Wagner value learning with softmax choice, noisy win-stay lose-shift and random or biased responding as competing models of the same choices.

title: The information contract of a predictive model
description: What is observed, what is predicted, what history is available in training and at inference, whether the person, task and period are familiar or unseen, the simplest baseline, and which claims remain untested.
